properties.Service_Description: ACTS Hunger Prevention Center provides food assistance to enrolled households once per month. Depending on availability, households receive canned goods, rice, pasta, peanut butter and jelly, bread, cereal, meat or fish, fresh fruits and vegetables, and dairy. Non-clients are offered an emergency bag of food and information on enrollment. A home delivery program serves homebound seniors aged 65 and older and people whose disability prevents them from coming in person, with deliveries once a month. ACTS is a Capital Area Food Bank partner participating in USDA programs, and partners with the Greater DC Diaper Bank to provide diapers and infant supplies. Services are offered in English and Spanish.
properties.Hours_of_Service: Food distribution: Monday 9-11:30 a.m. and 1-3 p.m.; Tuesday 1-3:30 p.m. and 5-7 p.m.; Thursday 9-11:30 a.m. and 1-3 p.m.; Friday CLOSED. New client enrollment: 1st and 2nd Wednesdays 10 a.m.-12:45 p.m.; 3rd and 4th Tuesdays 5-6:30 p.m. Follows the federal holiday schedule.
properties.How_to_Access_Services: Walk-in during distribution hours; no appointment needed. New clients must enroll in person during enrollment hours (arrive by 12:45 p.m. on Wednesdays). Only the applicant should enter the lobby; children may accompany them. New clients receive a starter order on the day they enroll and their first full order the following month.
properties.Photo_ID_Required: Yes. New clients must present photo identification showing a current address, or photo ID plus a bill or lease proving Eastern Prince William County residency (Dale City, Dumfries, Lake Ridge, Montclair, Occoquan, Quantico, Triangle, Woodbridge). Heads of household must present some form of ID. Additional information is requested but not required, and is used to determine USDA eligibility.

properties.Service_Description: Provides food-insecurity programs for Prince William County children and families, including the C.H.O.W. Wagon, mobile food distribution, school food pantries, and the Backpack Buddy Box program, which provides weekend meals to children during the school year. The Foundation also connects residents with local food-assistance partners when additional help is needed.
properties.Hours_of_Service: Varies by program, distribution site, and event.
properties.How_to_Access_Services: Access varies by program. Residents may participate through scheduled community/school distributions or contact the Foundation for current program information. The website also lists local food-assistance referral options for residents needing immediate food support.

properties.Service_Description: Provides food assistance and connections to basic-needs resources for individuals and families experiencing food insecurity.
properties.How_to_Access_Services: Walk-in, appointment, referral, or virtual access depending on the service. Contact Sahara Programs for current availability.
